subject: Resolutions B1 to B4 today at the 6P meeting on August 13, 2024
comment: Dear council, I am a business owner and resident in the Fairpark area of SLC. I support whole heartedly the approval of grants to provide additional workforce to agencies that assist with the issues impacting our community. I'm especially concerned by what is happening on 800 W between North Temple & 200 West. The loitering is growing by the day, along with overnight camping, drug use, & prostitution, which I have seen on 700 West just feet away from my front door. Please provide us with the funds, support, grants, what ever is possible to help us save our neighborhood. Thank you, Lucy Cardenas

subject: Just in case my comment cannot be heard in person - CIP support comments
comment: CIP Support Public Comment 8_13_24 I want to express gratitude for the ways the recommended CIP budget is supporting communities through prioritizing community spaces. I'm grateful for the city providing a way for constituents like me with a method to convey my priorities as a west side salt lake city resident through the Constituent CIP process. As a nearly 8 year poplar grove resident, mom of 3 young kids, regular user of the Jordan River Trail, who works and lives in Salt Lake City, who loves this city and my beautiful west side neighborhood and as someone who hopes to have Salt Lake City as a home for me and my family for a very long time, public family focused play space projects are critical. The heart of cities are the living, breathing parks, the respites from busy lives.It's one of the first things I notice, even seek out when visiting a new city. Moms, dads, caregivers, find connection and community support in beautiful, well kept public space,spaces that don't necessarily boqt the fanciest facilities and laundry list of amenities, but the spaces that are clearly loved and cared for. Me and many of my neighbors near 600 S and 1000 west look forward to the day that a playground is installed in a currently virtually unused area, which I recently learned was promised a playground years ago from real estate companies in the then new neighborhood. A promise that, like far too many other west side projects, has gone unfulfilled and eventually abandoned. I hope and look forward to seeing the fulfillment of promised projects such as Jordan River improvements, the Glendale Regional Park (now about a year and a half behind schedule), continued commitment to the urban forest on SLC's west side, and other such projects. I ask, make these west side projects a priority for you, our city's leaders & decision makers in the form of tangible outcomes. I look forward to the council showing love and care for the spaces we, the west side residents, including those with families, care for deeply.

subject: comment regarding raising the city council compensation
comment: Hello, I am writing today in support of raising pay for city council. I think it is important that people from all backgrounds are able to serve in city council and that pay should not be what keeps the most qualified person from running. I also believe that if we want the best to represent us we should pay them what they are worth, not try to underpay and hope that people are willing to make personal sacrifices to serve their community. If we want the best we have to pay for it. Thank you, Lucy Gelb

subject: Trail through Bonneville golf course
comment: It would be nice to have a way for people on bikes and walking to get through Bonneville golf course from Wasatch Drive to Foothill. I know there was a study about this a while ago, but nothing was done. When we could be a connector from the end of the Michigan Ave., Circle through the edge of the golf course. Another way could be through the back of the tennis courts down the gully and through to Foothill. thank you for taking this into account.

subject: Funding for Memory Grove
comment: I am hoping there will be support for funding for improvements in Memory Grove and City Creek Parks which are well used by citizens and visitors. I'm particularly concerned about the monuments which need refurbishing, landscaping in several areas and safety on the west switchbacks leading to and from East Capitol Boulevard. Kathryn Wright

subject: Homeless Housing Issue
comment: I am writing this mail to you with a possible resolution in mind for housing the homeless population in Salt Lake City. It has been brought to my attention that 4 elementary schools in the city were closed at the end of this past school year. Those schools have many independent rooms for classes, restrooms, kitchens, and heating systems. Security should also be easily made available. Parking for staff should not be a problem either. Why not use the recourses already available to you, instead of building new and expensive buildings? Concerned Civil Servant

subject: Rezoning at the mouth of emigration canyon
comment: Hi Kristina, I'm a resident in SL County and have grave concerns about a rezoning application that is going to the City's Planning Commission for higher density housing at the mouth of Emigration Canyon. The road has long been studied and this type of rezoning would only add to the risks on that road as well as to the residents in that canyon. There are a number of events that close one lane of traffic each year, along with it being a regular cycling route for cyclists. The road is at capacity and there aren't currently any public transit options near the area that would justify more density. Please be wise in considering this location as the zoo and craft markets at this is the place monument are also City attractions that create congestion in the area. The natural landmarks don't allow for widening or changing the road drastically. Camille Erickson
